question: If I wrap a program in a module that samples several rollouts and then keeps only the best one, why can the final DSPy trace show just one candidate run, and which run is preserved?
gold_answer: `dspy.Predict` traces each underlying predictor call, but `BestOfN` and the rollout loop inside `Refine` deliberately isolate each candidate under a temporary `trace=[]`, copy that rollout's trace, score it, and only splice back the currently best rollout at the end. So you do not get a concatenated trace of every candidate run. In `Refine`, helper predictor calls outside that temporary context can still appear separately, while reward-function tracing is excluded because the rollout trace is copied before scoring.

rubric.statement: When tracing is enabled, each `dspy.Predict` call records a trace entry by appending `(predictor, inputs, Prediction)` to `dspy.settings.trace`.
`BestOfN.forward` runs every sampled rollout inside `dspy.context(trace=[])`, so each candidate gets a fresh temporary trace instead of directly accumulating into the surrounding trace.

In `BestOfN`, the rollout trace is copied before `reward_fn` runs, `best_trace` is updated only for a better reward, and only `best_trace` is extended back at the end; this means the preserved candidate trace is just the current best rollout, not all candidates or reward-function activity.
`Refine.forward` uses the same per-rollout isolation pattern: each candidate runs under `dspy.context(trace=[])`, and that rollout trace is copied before `reward_fn` executes.

In `Refine`, only the rollout stored in `best_trace` is preserved among the sampled candidates, because `best_trace` changes only when `reward > best_reward` and is appended to `dspy.settings.trace` once after the rollout loop.

`Refine` generates feedback with `dspy.Predict(OfferFeedback)` after the temporary rollout-trace block, so these helper predictor calls can appear separately in the final trace even though only one candidate rollout is kept.
